en: <1>A delimited exclusivity</1> Only the cube receives the outline of the exclusivity under examination. The other dimensions remain separate from that outline. The background is neutral. It does not automatically represent the public domain.

Geometric language added on 15/11/2026 and redone on 16/11/2026. It is a later addition to the thesis, which does not propose a geometric ontology of intellectual property. <1>How to read the geometric language</1>.

<1>Four dimensions</1> From left to right, cube for expression, sphere for technical solution, cylinder for ornament and pyramid for distinctiveness. Each dimension comes with a band of use. The shapes are conventions and do not automatically amount to rights.
<1>The armor as an object</1> The same canonical armor, in front view. No new distinctive sign, mechanism or ornament was added.

<1>Separate dimensions</1> Beside the armor, cube and sphere above, cylinder and pyramid below, for expression, technical solution, ornament and distinctiveness. They are questions of analysis, not four presumed protections. The appearance of the skin does not prove a technical function.

<1>Protection and control of use</1> Beside the armor, two situations with the same protected cube. Above, the band of use is continuous. Below, the platform's dashed boundary interrupts the band. Control over use is shown separately from the protection under examination.

<1>Expression and functioning</1> The cube has the outline of the protection of the expression under examination. The sphere, shown separately, represents functioning. Being outside this outline does not mean the absence of any other protection.
<1>Ornament</1> The cylinder presents a surface that can receive an ornamental configuration. The band represents use. The incidence of protection is not presumed.
<1>Distinctiveness</1> The pyramid represents the distinctive dimension. The blue band represents use. It is not an arrow of identification of origin.

<1>Surface and pattern</1> The same pattern appears on the curved surface and on the open plane. The double outline delimits the pattern examined in this example, without declaring protection of the whole object.

<1>Sign and origin</1> The pyramid relates to a point of origin through a thin arrow. The blue band, wide and without a tip, represents use. This piece teaches the relation of identification, without presuming the existence or scope of a trademark right.
<1>Continuous use</1> The double outline delimits the protection represented. The band of use remains continuous.
<1>Interrupted use</1> The protection stays the same. The platform's dashed boundary interrupts the band of use.

<1>The name does not change the relationship</1> The empty label represents the contractual designation, explained here as a license. It is attached to the platform's boundary. The outline of protection stays the same, while the band of use appears interrupted. The label contains no writing.

<1>Protection and outcomes</1> The object with an outline of protection appears beside other shapes, grouped as possible outcomes. The band of use remains continuous. The composition introduces the discussion of social purpose.

<1>Preserving continuity</1> On the left, the protected object is inside the platform's dashed boundary. On the right, the boundary disappears, but the object and its protection remain. The band of use continues in both situations. The drawing presents the continuity to be examined, not an automatic technical or legal solution.

<1>Dimensions of the same object</1> Cube, sphere, cylinder and pyramid stand apart, linked to the same band of use. They represent dimensions of a common object. The absence of protection outlines in this introduction avoids presuming that every regime applies automatically.

How to read the geometric language

The shapes on this page are conventions of explanation, and not a geometric classification proposed by the thesis. Start with a distinction. The dimension of an object, the scope of an exclusivity and the control exercised by the platform are different things.
The four shapes
<1>Cube</1> Expression
<1>Sphere</1> Technical solution
<1>Cylinder</1> Ornament
<1>Pyramid</1> Distinctiveness
Recognizing a shape does not allow the conclusion that legal protection exists. Whether a right applies depends on the case and its requirements.
Lines that say different things
Double outline
Scope of the exclusivity examined in that example.
Dashed boundary
Contractual or technical control by the platform.
Wide band without a tip
Use or functional outcome. A gap indicates interruption.
Thin arrow with a tip
Relation of identification of origin.
Page background
Neutral space. It does not automatically mean the public domain.
An example of reading

The cube keeps its double outline. The platform's dashed boundary crosses the band of use, which appears interrupted. The image distinguishes the protection of the object from the control over its use.
The armor in sequence
Relations

<1>The workings inside</1> The whole sphere appears on the left. On the right, the internal organization is exposed by two gears. There is no outline of incidence. The drawing presents functioning, without presuming legal protection of the mechanism.

<1>Control beyond the cut</1> The double outline of exclusivity stays close to the cube. Two dashed boundaries show the extension of the platform's control, until it encloses other dimensions and use. The outline of protection does not turn into control. They are distinct elements.

<1>The delimitation is added</1> First, the cube appears without an outline of incidence. Then the same cube receives a double outline. Use remains continuous. The sequence represents the construction of a delimitation, without asserting the absence of other protections in the first situation.
